relations.quote: The tape layout reorders address bits so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) on several axes runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis, which is where the transform's cost drops below the standard pass count.

The tape layout reorders address bits so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) on several axes runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis, which is where the transform's cost drops below the standard pass count.
This is at most $Dq-1$ exchanges, each done by the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) in $O(TpK^\tau)$ even for nonadjacent chunks

By [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md) the forward transform leaves its outputs in bit-reversed order, written $B$ here (the bit-reversal permutation on all axes), and the opposite transform consumes that order, so no reordering is executed.

derivations.quote: Adding the three costs, the moves, exchanges and rounds give $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
